fields.description_1: DCA Dienstverlening had to help organisations identify the right cleaning or specialist service and move toward a quotation. The website covers office and hotel cleaning, floor care, façade work, industrial cleaning, construction handover, drone cleaning and inspections, so the offer is broad. Visitors need to understand which service fits the location, what the company can handle and how to request help without reading every page first. The project therefore needed strong service grouping, trust information and visible next steps. Mobile users needed the same hierarchy when comparing services or opening the quotation route. The portfolio text also had to stay factual, using the current public service offer without inventing conversion results, customer outcomes or operational improvements that were not independently verified.
fields.description_2: For DCA Dienstverlening, I structured the WordPress experience around cleaning categories, specialist services, proof, practical information and quotation actions. The homepage presents the broad offer first, then separates regular cleaning, specialist cleaning and drone services so organisations can reach the relevant route. Reviews, client logos and working-method content support trust without replacing the service explanation. Quotation and contact actions stay close to the sections where a visitor is likely to decide. The same hierarchy is preserved on mobile, with service choices and calls to action easy to scan. This gives the portfolio entry a clear account of the actual website and current service range without adding unsupported claims about lead growth, customer satisfaction or other measured outcomes.

fields.description_1: ACF Image Auto Filler had to reduce repetitive image assignment without making unsafe assumptions about complex ACF structures. Editors may map many Media Library images to normal ACF Image fields or featured images, but bulk writes can overwrite values or target the wrong content when mapping is unclear. Repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clone fields add ambiguity, so the plugin deliberately does not auto-fill them. The workflow needed preview mapping, overwrite confirmation, manual mapping, batch limits, rollback and an audit trail. The portfolio text also had to explain that no content is sent to external services. The challenge was controlled bulk editing: make image work faster while keeping supported field types, permissions and recovery options explicit.
fields.description_2: I built ACF Image Auto Filler as a WordPress admin workflow that starts with selected content, supported fields and Media Library images, then shows the mapping before any write. Top-level ACF Image fields are supported, along with direct Image fields inside Groups when enabled, and featured images can be handled separately. Existing values are skipped unless overwrite is explicitly enabled. Manual mapping, batch mode and CSV dry-run export add control when automatic order is not enough. Saved runs can retain rollback data for the current user, while an admin audit log records operations. Capability and per-item permission checks protect bulk actions. Repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clones remain excluded, keeping the solution bounded instead of guessing how complex nested data should be written.

fields.description_1: Wehear4u had to help visitors understand a humanitarian hearing-care mission and see how they could contribute. The organisation supports children and adults with hearing problems, including work in Kenya, and promotes used hearing-aid donations, financial support and partnerships. That creates several audiences: someone may want to understand the mission, donate equipment, support a trip, become a collection point or share the initiative. The website needed to connect the human story with practical participation without turning every section into a donation request. Mobile visitors also needed a clear route through mission information and actions. The portfolio text had to remain respectful and factual, avoiding invented impact numbers or medical claims beyond the organisation's publicly described work and goals.
fields.description_2: For Wehear4u, I structured the WordPress presentation around the mission, the people the initiative aims to support and practical ways visitors can help. Story and purpose come first, followed by routes for donating hearing aids, contributing financially, becoming a partner or learning about the work in Kenya. Calls to action connect naturally to the surrounding content instead of competing on every section. The same priorities stay visible on mobile so emotional storytelling and practical information remain readable together. The project story shows how the website supports awareness and participation without overstating measured outcomes. It keeps the hearing-care focus understandable to donors, partners and general visitors while leaving medical impact claims to the organisation and its qualified partners.

fields.description_1: Fidelyaa had to explain a consultancy offer spanning strategic advice, guidance, reintegration and activation programmes, tenders, analysis and implementation support. Government organisations and SMEs may arrive with different problems, so one generic consultancy message would not explain where each service fits. The website needed to separate the main routes while showing that they belong to one advisory approach. Visitors also needed enough context to distinguish strategy, programme support and implementation before starting a conversation. The case study therefore had to describe the actual consultancy work in plain English rather than rely on broad words such as expertise or solutions. Mobile structure and contact routes needed the same clarity, and the portfolio text had to avoid outcomes that were not measured or publicly supported.
fields.description_2: For Fidelyaa, I structured the WordPress presentation around the main advisory and programme areas, with separate context for strategy, guidance, reintegration, activation, tenders, analysis and implementation. This helps government organisations and SMEs move from a specific question toward the relevant part of the offer. Service explanations stay concise, while supporting context shows how advice and execution relate without collapsing them into one generic proposition. Contact routes remain visible after the relevant information so a conversation follows naturally from the service being considered. I used direct headings and simple English to keep the case understandable to non-specialists. The solution describes the real information architecture and consultancy scope without adding unsupported claims about client outcomes, programme effectiveness or business growth.

fields.description_1: SooCool for WooCommerce had to connect ecommerce orders with an external transport platform without creating duplicate fulfilment work or unsafe order-state changes. Shipping integrations handle customer and delivery data, remote API calls, labels, delivery moments and status updates, so failures can affect operations and WooCommerce records. Retries must not blindly create a second transport order, and webhook messages need verification. The plugin also required HPOS-compatible order access, background processing and explicit checkout boundaries. The portfolio text therefore had to explain the engineering problem rather than present the integration as a simple API connection. The key challenge was keeping WooCommerce and the logistics provider synchronized while protecting credentials, personal data, replay-sensitive webhooks and ambiguous remote states from uncontrolled fulfilment changes.
fields.description_2: I built SooCool for WooCommerce around controlled order submission, delivery scheduling, status handling, retries and shipping-label workflows. Order access uses WooCommerce APIs so the integration remains HPOS-compatible instead of relying on legacy post storage. Remote submissions can run asynchronously, and existing transport orders are linked instead of recreated blindly. Webhooks use timestamped HMAC verification and replay protection before they can influence local state. Ambiguous remote statuses do not overwrite WooCommerce orders automatically, while retries and maintenance recovery handle temporary failures. API credentials are masked and logs avoid intentionally storing complete sensitive payloads. Delivery-moment selection is validated server-side. The solution shows the real integration boundaries and failure handling without claiming that external logistics becomes error-free or every checkout implementation has proven feature parity.

fields.description_1: Content Sync Manager had to make large WordPress content and media updates reviewable before they become bulk writes. Pages, posts, WooCommerce products, custom post types, ACF fields and media information can be spread across many editing screens. Import workflows add risk because an incorrect file can overwrite structured content, rename media or touch builder references. The project therefore needed preview binding, validation, permission checks, backups and explicit confirmation around higher-risk operations. Media filename changes also required a usage scan so fixed URLs or inaccessible pages could block unsafe renames. The portfolio text needed to show this safety model instead of describing generic automation. The central problem was efficient bulk editing without turning convenience into uncontrolled changes across a WordPress installation.
fields.description_2: I built Content Sync Manager as an admin-only workflow for controlled export, review, import and recovery of WordPress content and media. It supports pages, posts, WooCommerce products and supported custom content while dynamically detecting relevant ACF fields. Imports are validated before writes, then tied to the reviewed source so a different file cannot silently replace the approved preview. Backups and recovery paths support rollback. Media workflows include usage context, ACF paths and guarded filename changes; renaming fails closed when builder metadata, unsupported storage or incomplete permissions make references unsafe to update. Higher-risk actions require capability checks and confirmation. The solution lets teams handle larger structured updates while preserving a clear boundary between reviewing proposed changes and modifying live WordPress content.

fields.description_1: The WooCommerce Egaline Calculator had to turn project measurements into a product quantity customers could actually order. Material purchases may depend on area, layer thickness, kilograms per square metre, bag weight and product variation, so a normal quantity field cannot explain how much is required. The calculation also needed to stay connected to live pricing, discounts, tax handling and the cart instead of producing an isolated estimate. Invalid numerical inputs or inconsistent dependencies could create confusing quantities. The portfolio text therefore needed to explain the customer-facing calculation problem, not an abstract internal tool. The challenge was linking technical material rules with a simple WooCommerce buying flow that preserves calculated information through product selection, cart and order processing.
fields.description_2: I built the Egaline Calculator directly into the WooCommerce product journey before the add-to-cart action. Customers enter project measurements such as area and thickness, while the plugin calculates the required material quantity and updates related values in real time. Product-specific settings define bag weight, material density, calculation mode and optional discount thresholds. The calculator supports simple and variable products, keeps calculation data with the cart item and preserves it in the order. Input validation prevents invalid numerical values from becoming purchase quantities, while WooCommerce remains responsible for normal tax and pricing behaviour. The responsive interface keeps controls usable on smaller screens. The solution connects domain-specific measurement rules to an actual ecommerce transaction instead of leaving the calculation separate from purchasing.

fields.description_1: Exam Registration Manager had to make examination sign-up clearer than handling dates, candidate details and registration status through disconnected forms or manual administration. An exam workflow combines scheduled sessions, available places, participant information and confirmation steps, so the interface must show what can be selected and what is required before submission. Administrators also need a structured way to review registrations without turning normal content screens into an improvised booking database. The project therefore needed clear boundaries between public registration and back-office management. The portfolio text had to describe that workflow without inventing pass rates, registration growth or other unmeasured results. The main problem was practical coordination: connect exam dates and participant registration in one manageable WordPress process.
fields.description_2: I structured Exam Registration Manager around a dedicated WordPress registration flow for exam sessions and participant information. The public side guides candidates from an available exam option to the fields needed for a complete registration, keeping the next action visible. Administrative views organise submitted registrations so staff can review the relevant session and participant details from one workflow. Validation is applied before information is accepted, and exam-related records stay separate from normal page content. Clear labels and compact steps keep the process understandable on desktop and mobile. The portfolio solution focuses on the real management problem the plugin addresses: coordinating exam scheduling and registration inside WordPress, without claiming educational outcomes, registration growth or operational improvements that were not verified through project evidence.

fields.description_1: Services Overview Manager had to solve a content problem created when services are maintained as scattered page sections or manual lists. As the offer grows, categories, summaries, prices and related details can become inconsistent, while visitors lack a place to search or filter what is available. The plugin therefore needed a dedicated service content model that editors could maintain independently from presentation. Import and export also had to stay controlled because CSV changes can affect many records at once. The public interface needed lightweight search and category filtering without loading unnecessary assets site-wide. The portfolio text had to explain this content problem rather than present a generic service page. The challenge was maintaining one service source while keeping the frontend overview easy to browse.
fields.description_2: I built Services Overview Manager around a dedicated WordPress service post type, categories and structured metadata. Editors can maintain services in one content model instead of updating repeated manual lists across pages. A reusable shortcode renders the public overview with search and category filtering, giving visitors a clearer way to narrow the offer. Controlled CSV import and export support updates, while nonces, capability checks, sanitization and upload validation protect those actions. Frontend and admin assets are scoped to where they are needed, and uninstall behaviour remains conservative. The solution separates service data from layout while still giving the public site a searchable presentation. The portfolio case explains the actual architecture and management workflow without claiming traffic, lead or conversion improvements that were not independently measured.

fields.description_1: Sparx Entertainment Agency had to help people planning weddings, birthdays or corporate events explore a broad entertainment catalogue without losing the route to an enquiry. The offer includes DJs, live musicians, bands, special acts and event extras, so visitors may start with an event type rather than a specific performer. A flat list would make different options difficult to compare and separate inspiration from booking intent. The website therefore needed clear entertainment categories, enough context to understand each direction and visible contact routes near relevant choices. Mobile browsing also mattered because image-heavy entertainment content can become cumbersome on small screens. The portfolio text had to describe the actual offer in simple English, avoiding invented booking figures or audience-response claims that were not measured.
fields.description_2: For Sparx Entertainment Agency, I structured the WordPress experience around entertainment types and event needs. Visitors can move from broad choices such as DJs or live music into specific artists, bands, special acts and supporting extras without returning to a generic overview each time. Visual content provides inspiration, while short descriptions explain each category and enquiry actions remain close to the options being considered. The hierarchy keeps the entertainment catalogue central rather than burying it beneath agency marketing text. Responsive layouts preserve the same discovery route on smaller screens, where images, category cards and contact actions need clear priority. The solution shows how a broad creative offer became an understandable booking-oriented structure without adding unsupported claims about enquiries, conversion rates or commercial performance.
